patterns: APPSC asks APRA 2014 as pure number/structure recall: 12 Parts, 108 Sections, 13 Schedules; 'which Part deals with X' (Part V revenue, Part VIII services, Part XII amends Arts 371D/168); Section 8 Governor and common capital; appointed day 2 June 2014.

Mulki/regional-agitation questions are cause-effect one-steppers: Jai Andhra caused by the SC Mulki judgment; ended by the Six-Point Formula; President's Rule 1973 due to Jai Andhra; Six-Point given effect by the 32nd Amendment (traps: 33rd, 'abolition of Mulki rules', 'repression').
State-formation items are chronological-order or year-matching (Haryana 1966 -> Meghalaya/Tripura 1972 -> Karnataka rename 1973; J&K/Ladakh UTs 2019); APPSC does not go into Acts' clause details.
Distractors in PYQs are near-miss dates (March/June/July 2014) and neighbouring Part/Section numbers; the app mirrors this well with Part/Section one-liners.

The app over-reaches into clause numbers of the 1969/1972 formulas, Gorkhaland chronology, 2026 amendments and opinion-style 'criticism' items, none of which have PYQ precedent; its multi-statement UPSC-style items are heavier than APPSC's single-fact questions.
